title: Maximum Score of a Good Subarray
summary: Given an array of integers and an integer k, find the maximum score of a subarray where the score is the minimum value in the subarray multiplied by its length, and the subarray must include the k-th element.
statement: Given an array of integers and an integer k, find the maximum score of a subarray where the score is the minimum value in the subarray multiplied by its length, and the subarray must include the k-th element.
constraints: A good contiguous subarray must include index k.
Its score is its minimum value times its length; return the maximum score.
reference_solution:
def maximum_good_subarray_score(nums, k):
 left=right=k;minimum=nums[k];answer=minimum
 while left>0 or right+1<len(nums):
  if left==0:right+=1
  elif right+1==len(nums):left-=1
  elif nums[left-1]>nums[right+1]:left-=1
  else:right+=1
  minimum=min(minimum,nums[left],nums[right]);answer=max(answer,minimum*(right-left+1))
 return answer

hints: Grow an interval outward from k while tracking its minimum.
When both sides are available, expand toward the larger adjacent value.
Update the running minimum and score after every expansion until the whole array is covered.
For every possible minimum threshold, choosing the larger boundary delays lowering that minimum and visits the widest qualifying interval, so no optimal score is skipped.
